title: Ionic Memory and Computing
intro: At the molecular scale, ion transport through a pore can depend on its previous electrical history. We use simulations to understand how molecular interactions create memory and signaling behavior, and to explore physical principles for ionic computing.
caption: Conceptual comparison of biological signaling and ionic computing.
background_html: Growing demand for computing motivates the search for more energy-efficient ways to process information. Biological nervous systems offer inspiration: they process information through ionic signals and connections that retain a memory of past activity.

title: Selective Ion Transport
intro: Biological ion channels show that selectivity can coexist with rapid transport. We study how pore chemistry, molecular interactions, and membrane motion control ion passage, seeking principles for selective membranes and resource recovery.
caption: Bio-inspired selective transport for rare-earth separation.
background_html: Selective separation is essential to clean water and the recovery of valuable elements, including rare-earth elements. Separating chemically similar ions remains a fundamental challenge: an interaction strong enough to capture a desired ion can also make it difficult to release.

title: Interfacial Molecular Recognition
intro: We use molecular simulations to understand how interfaces influence biomolecular motion and recognition. By connecting these insights with experiments, we aim to establish physical principles for designing receptor–electrode interfaces for chemical and biological sensing.
caption: Molecular recognition in biological sensing and electrochemical biosensors.
background_html: Electrochemical biosensors offer a route to detecting disease biomarkers near the point of care by converting molecular recognition into electrical signals. Yet a receptor that binds a target in solution may behave differently when attached to an electrode. The surrounding surface can change both the receptor’s shape and the molecules available to bind it.
